```{webr}
#| include: false
#| autorun: true
# Lab machinery – the specification menu, its validation, and the helpers of
# Tasks 4 and 5: try_spec(), my_experiments(), submit_exploration(), prereg(),
# build_model(), run_spec() and report_result(). Every result is read from the
# curve of 864 specifications in spec_curve.csv, and every option that is
# not on the curve is refused with the reason recorded in menu_options.csv;
# both files arrive with the page through its `resources:` list, in the folder
# that the setup cell of the including page names as .data_dir (data/ in the
# lab, cases/eu-frames/data/ in the live deck of the short session). These helpers
# fit no model in the browser, so the only estimation package on the page is
# fixest, which Task 3 uses for two of its reproductions; the third, of
# 018OL, installs lme4 and lmerTest when it is first run. The workspace fits the same
# specifications live, with their CR2 test (clubSandwich), and returns the same
# numbers.
.curve   <- utils::read.csv(file.path(.data_dir, "spec_curve.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) # r-style: keep – readr would add 4 MB to the download
.options <- utils::read.csv(file.path(.data_dir, "menu_options.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE, # r-style: keep – as above
                            encoding = "UTF-8")
.course_url <- "https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds-eu"

# The thirteen axis codes that key the curve, in its column order; the
# inference rule is the fourteenth decision and is the same for every row.
.axis_codes <- c("outcome", "predictor", "copredictor", "estimator", "sample", "weights",
                 "construction", "noop", "item_set", "cell_weight", "measure", "pred_form",
                 "family")
.neg_framings <- c("mcomm", "mlib", "mneg")

# The options that the curve keeps, in the three groups of the menu: the
# question, its measurement and the model. Every other option of the menu is
# listed in menu_options.csv.
.menu <- list(
  # The question
  my_outcome      = c("mcosmo", "mutil", "mpos"),
  my_predictor    = c("unemp", "growth"),
  my_copredictor  = c("none", "other"),
  my_estimator    = c("fe_twoway", "fe_country"),
  my_sample       = "all",
  my_weights      = "none",
  my_construction = "share",
  # Measurement
  my_noop         = c("zero", "drop"),
  my_item_set     = c("all", "un"),
  my_cell_weight  = c("unweighted", "design"),
  my_measure      = c("wb_nat", "es_1574_act", "es_2064_pop", "es_2564_lfs", "wb_growth"),
  # The model
  my_pred_form    = c("raw", "log"),
  my_family       = "gaussian",
  my_se           = "cr2"
)
.measures_for <- list(unemp  = c("wb_nat", "es_1574_act", "es_2064_pop", "es_2564_lfs"),
                      growth = "wb_growth")

if (nrow(.curve) != 864 ||
    !all(purrr::map_lgl(.axis_codes, \(a) all(.curve[[a]] %in% .menu[[paste0("my_", a)]]))))
  stop("The curve of 864 specifications did not load as expected. Reload the page.",
       call. = FALSE)
.curve_keys <- purrr::exec(paste, !!!unname(as.list(.curve[.axis_codes])), sep = "|")

.est_lab <- function(e) c(
  fe_twoway  = "two-way fixed effects (country + year)",
  fe_country = "country fixed effects")[[e]]
.se_lab <- "CR2 errors clustered by country, Satterthwaite df"

# The term for the claim-carrying predictor as it appears in a formula:
# log(unemp) when the log form is chosen, else the bare variable name.
.main_term <- function(ch) {
  if (ch$my_predictor == "unemp" && ch$my_pred_form == "log") "log(unemp)"
  else ch$my_predictor
}
.copred_term <- function(ch) if (identical(ch$my_predictor, "unemp")) "growth" else "unemp"

# --- validation ------------------------------------------------------------
# Two entry points into the same rules. .validate() takes a named list, which
# is how the exploratory try_spec() supplies its arguments; .check_choices()
# reads the fourteen my_* choices and claim_align out of the session, which is
# how the declared flow reads the preregistration cell. An option that is not
# on the curve stops with the reason from menu_options.csv, the page of the
# course that teaches it, and the options that stay on the curve.
.page_titles <- c(
  "companion/measurement.qmd"      = "The items behind the scales",
  "companion/panel-data.qmd"       = "Panel data",
  "companion/multilevel.qmd"       = "Multilevel models",
  "companion/dags.qmd"             = "Causal graphs",
  "companion/multiverse.qmd"       = "The multiverse and its critics",
  "companion/weighting.qmd"        = "Weights",
  "companion/missingness.qmd"      = "Missing answers",
  "companion/data-sources.qmd"     = "Social science data sources",
  "cases/eu-frames/multiverse.qmd" = "Multiverse",
  "cases/eu-frames/map.qmd"        = "Decision map")
.page_ref <- function(path) {
  title <- if (path %in% names(.page_titles)) .page_titles[[path]] else path
  sprintf("%s, %s/%s", title, .course_url, sub("\\.qmd$", ".html", path))
}
.or_list <- function(x) {
  q <- paste0("\"", x, "\"")
  if (length(q) == 1) q else paste(paste(q[-length(q)], collapse = ", "), "or", q[length(q)])
}
# two older option codes that labels and calls may still use, mapped to the rows that hold their reasons
.legacy <- c("se:clustered" = "cr1", "weights:n_cy" = "n_cell")

.on_menu <- function(k, v) is.character(v) && length(v) == 1 && !is.na(v) && v %in% .menu[[k]]

.refuse <- function(k, v, ch, as_args) {
  shown <- function(a) if (as_args) a else paste0("my_", a)
  axis  <- sub("^my_", "", k)
  keep  <- if (k == "my_measure" && isTRUE(ch$my_predictor %in% names(.measures_for)))
    .measures_for[[ch$my_predictor]] else .menu[[k]]
  map   <- paste0("  Every decision and its options: ", .page_ref("cases/eu-frames/map.qmd"))
  if (!is.character(v) || length(v) != 1 || is.na(v))
    stop(sprintf("%s needs one option in quotes, for example %s = \"%s\".",
                 shown(axis), shown(axis), .menu[[k]][1]), call. = FALSE)
  look <- if (paste0(axis, ":", v) %in% names(.legacy)) .legacy[[paste0(axis, ":", v)]] else v
  row  <- .options[.options$axis == axis & .options$option == look & !.options$on_curve, ]
  msg <- if (nrow(row) == 1) c(
    sprintf("%s = \"%s\" (%s) is not on the curve of 864 specifications, so it has no result here.",
            shown(axis), v, row$label),
    paste0("  Why: ", row$reason),
    if (axis == "se")
      "  Inference is fixed: every result on the curve is tested by CR2 errors clustered by country with Satterthwaite df, and the printout gives the conventional t beside it.",
    paste0("  Where it is taught: ", .page_ref(row$taught_on)),
    map,
    sprintf("  To stay on the curve, choose %s = %s.", shown(axis), .or_list(keep))
  ) else c(
    sprintf("%s = \"%s\" is not an option on the menu.", shown(axis), v),
    sprintf("  On the curve: %s.", paste(.menu[[k]], collapse = " | ")),
    if (any(.options$axis == axis & !.options$on_curve))
      sprintf("  Off the curve, refused with the reason why: %s.",
              paste(.options$option[.options$axis == axis & !.options$on_curve], collapse = " | ")),
    map
  )
  stop(paste(msg, collapse = "\n"), call. = FALSE)
}

.validate <- function(ch, as_args = FALSE) {
  shown <- function(a) if (as_args) a else paste0("my_", a)
  # the co-predictor may also be named by its variable, growth or unemp
  if (identical(ch$my_copredictor, .copred_term(ch)))
    ch <- utils::modifyList(ch, list(my_copredictor = "other"))
  bad <- purrr::discard(names(.menu), \(k) .on_menu(k, ch[[k]]))
  if (length(bad) > 0) .refuse(bad[1], ch[[bad[1]]], ch, as_args)
  if (ch$my_predictor == "growth" && ch$my_pred_form == "log")
    stop(sprintf("GDP growth enters raw only – it takes negative values, so its log is undefined. Use %s = \"raw\".",
                 shown("pred_form")), call. = FALSE)
  if (!ch$my_measure %in% .measures_for[[ch$my_predictor]])
    stop(sprintf("%s = \"%s\" is a series for %s; with %s = \"%s\" choose %s = %s.",
                 shown("measure"), ch$my_measure, setdiff(names(.measures_for), ch$my_predictor),
                 shown("predictor"), ch$my_predictor, shown("measure"),
                 .or_list(.measures_for[[ch$my_predictor]])), call. = FALSE)
  ch
}

.check_choices <- function() {
  need <- names(.menu)
  missing <- purrr::discard(need, \(k) exists(k))
  if (length(missing) > 0)
    stop("Not declared yet: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "),
         ". Fill in every choice in the preregistration cell and run it first.",
         call. = FALSE)
  if (!exists("claim_align"))
    stop("Also declare claim_align <- TRUE (the course convention) in the preregistration cell.",
         call. = FALSE)
  .validate(purrr::set_names(purrr::map(need, \(k) get(k)), need))
}

# --- the curve -------------------------------------------------------------
.key_of <- function(ch) paste(unlist(ch[paste0("my_", .axis_codes)]), collapse = "|")

.lookup <- function(ch) {
  i <- match(.key_of(ch), .curve_keys)
  if (is.na(i))
    stop("That specification passed the checks but is not among the 864 on the curve. This should not happen; tell the facilitator which call you ran.",
         call. = FALSE)
  .curve[i, ]
}

# One result in the form that the printout and the submission use: the
# conventional fit (b, se, t, df, r), the claim-aligned r, the CR2 test with its
# Satterthwaite df, and the placement among the 864.
.result <- function(ch) {
  hit <- .lookup(ch)
  list(b = hit$b, se = hit$se, t = hit$t, df = hit$df, n = hit$n_cells, r = hit$r,
       r_ca = hit$r_ca, p_cr2 = hit$p_cr2, df_cr2 = hit$df_cr2,
       placement = mean(.curve$r_ca < hit$r_ca),
       source = "read from the curve of 864 specifications")
}

# The claim-alignment factor. The claim expects framing to rise with growth,
# so a growth slope is reported with its sign flipped; the negative framings,
# which are not on the curve, were reverse-coded the same way. The r_ca column
# of the curve is r times this factor.
.flip <- function(ch)
  (if (ch$my_outcome %in% .neg_framings) -1 else 1) *
  (if (ch$my_predictor == "growth") -1 else 1)

# The one-line spec label that the class chart reads: six of the seven
# decisions about the question, then in brackets the scoring rule, the
# measurement decisions and the decisions about the model, with the inference
# rule last.
.spec_line <- function(ch) {
  neg <- ch$my_outcome %in% .neg_framings
  paste0(ch$my_outcome, if (neg) "_ca" else "", " ~ ", ch$my_predictor, "(", ch$my_pred_form, ")",
         if (ch$my_copredictor == "other") paste0(" + ", .copred_term(ch)) else "",
         " | ", ch$my_estimator, " | ", ch$my_sample, " | w:", ch$my_weights,
         " [", ch$my_construction, ", ", ch$my_noop, ", items:", ch$my_item_set, ", cells:",
         ch$my_cell_weight, ", ", ch$my_measure, " | ", ch$my_family, ", se:", ch$my_se, "]")
}

# four decimals, so that a p just above 0.05 never prints as 0.050
.fmt_p <- function(p) if (p < 0.001) "< 0.001" else sprintf("= %.4f", p)

.class_line <- function(res) {
  below <- res$r_ca < 0
  sig   <- res$p_cr2 < 0.05
  if (below && sig) "below zero and significant under CR2 (p < 0.05), in the direction of the claim"
  else if (below) "below zero, but not significant under CR2 (p >= 0.05)"
  else if (sig) "above zero and significant under CR2, against the direction of the claim"
  else "above zero and not significant under CR2"
}

.print_result <- function(ch, res, lead = NULL, aligned = TRUE) {
  fl <- if (aligned) .flip(ch) else 1
  writeLines(c(
    lead,
    paste0("  ", .spec_line(ch)),
    sprintf("  b = %.5f   se = %.5f   t = %.3f on %d df (conventional standard error)",
            fl * res$b, res$se, fl * res$t, round(res$df)),
    sprintf("  partial r = %.3f, %s", if (aligned) res$r_ca else res$r,
            if (aligned) "claim-aligned (below zero is the direction of the claim)"
            else "on the original scale of the outcome"),
    sprintf("  p %s with CR2 errors clustered by country, on %.1f Satterthwaite df",
            .fmt_p(res$p_cr2), res$df_cr2),
    paste0(if (aligned) "  Class: " else "  Class, on the claim-aligned scale: ", .class_line(res)),
    sprintf("  Placement: %.0f%% of the 864 specifications on the curve have a more negative claim-aligned r",
            100 * res$placement),
    if (aligned && ch$my_predictor == "growth")
      "  (growth: b, t and r are shown with their signs flipped, because the claim expects framing to rise with growth)",
    if (!aligned)
      "  (claim_align = FALSE: shown on the original scale; the class chart receives the claim-aligned values)",
    paste0("  (", res$source, ")")))
  invisible(res)
}

# --- Task 4: the exploratory helpers ---------------------------------------
.tried <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
assign("log", NULL, envir = .tried)
assign("last", NULL, envir = .tried)

try_spec <- function(outcome = "mcosmo", predictor = "unemp", copredictor = "none",
                     estimator = "fe_twoway", sample = "all", weights = "none",
                     construction = "share", noop = "zero", item_set = "all",
                     cell_weight = "unweighted", measure = NULL,
                     pred_form = "raw", family = "gaussian", se = "cr2") {
  if (is.null(measure)) measure <- if (identical(predictor, "growth")) "wb_growth" else "wb_nat"
  ch <- .validate(list(my_outcome = outcome, my_predictor = predictor, my_copredictor = copredictor,
                       my_estimator = estimator, my_sample = sample, my_weights = weights,
                       my_construction = construction, my_noop = noop, my_item_set = item_set,
                       my_cell_weight = cell_weight, my_measure = measure,
                       my_pred_form = pred_form, my_family = family, my_se = se), as_args = TRUE)
  res <- .result(ch)
  .print_result(ch, res, lead = "")
  fl  <- .flip(ch)
  row <- data.frame(stats::setNames(ch, sub("^my_", "", names(ch))), # r-style: keep – prints as the plain table of my_experiments()
                    b = fl * res$b, t = fl * res$t, r_aligned = res$r_ca, p_cr2 = res$p_cr2,
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  assign("log", purrr::list_rbind(list(.tried$log, row)), envir = .tried)
  assign("last", list(ch = ch, res = res), envir = .tried)
  invisible(row)
}

# The running log of everything try_spec() has looked up. Only the decisions
# that varied are shown; the constant ones are those of the reproduced
# specification or of every call.
my_experiments <- function() {
  d <- .tried$log
  if (is.null(d)) {
    writeLines("Nothing tried yet – call try_spec() at least once.")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  axes   <- sub("^my_", "", names(.menu))
  varied <- names(purrr::keep(d[axes], \(x) length(unique(x)) > 1))
  show <- d |>
    datawizard::data_select(select = c(varied, "b", "t", "r_aligned", "p_cr2")) |>
    datawizard::data_modify(b = signif(b, 3), t = round(t, 2), r_aligned = round(r_aligned, 3),
                            p_cr2 = round(p_cr2, 4))
  writeLines(sprintf("Specifications you have tried (%d):\n", nrow(d)))
  print(show, row.names = FALSE)
  writeLines(sprintf("\nSpread of claim-aligned r: %.3f to %.3f  |  below zero and significant under CR2: %d of %d",
                     min(d$r_aligned), max(d$r_aligned),
                     sum(d$r_aligned < 0 & d$p_cr2 < 0.05), nrow(d)))
  invisible(show)
}

submit_exploration <- function(nickname = NULL) {
  if (is.null(.tried$last))
    stop("Nothing to submit – call try_spec() first, ending with the specification you want on the chart.",
         call. = FALSE)
  .submit(.tried$last$ch, .tried$last$res, "explore",
          "Your exploratory submission (claim-aligned, the last specification you tried):",
          nickname)
}

# --- Task 5: the declared helpers ------------------------------------------

prereg <- function() {
  ch <- .check_choices()
  writeLines(c(
    "DECLARED – your preregistered specification, fixed before you run it:",
    "",
    "  The question",
    paste("    outcome    :", ch$my_outcome),
    paste0("    predictor  : ", ch$my_predictor,
           if (ch$my_predictor == "growth") " (claim-expected sign flipped automatically)"),
    paste("    adjusted   :", if (ch$my_copredictor == "other") .copred_term(ch) else "nothing"),
    paste("    estimator  :", .est_lab(ch$my_estimator)),
    paste("    sample     :", ch$my_sample, "   whose average:", ch$my_weights),
    paste("    scored as  :", ch$my_construction),
    "  Measurement",
    paste("    no-opinion rule:", ch$my_noop, "  items:", ch$my_item_set),
    paste("    cells:", ch$my_cell_weight, "  series:", ch$my_measure),
    "  The model",
    paste("    form:", ch$my_pred_form, "  family:", ch$my_family, "  inference:", .se_lab),
    paste("  claim_align:", isTRUE(claim_align)),
    "",
    "These choices are now fixed for the rest of the session – the later",
    "cells read them from the preregistration cell. Copy that cell into your",
    "notes: it is your preregistration record, made before you see the result."))
  invisible(ch)
}

build_model <- function(formula, estimator) {
  ch <- .check_choices()
  if (missing(formula) || !inherits(formula, "formula"))
    stop("The first argument must be a formula: outcome ~ predictor terms, unquoted.",
         call. = FALSE)
  lhs <- all.vars(formula[[2]])
  if (!identical(lhs, ch$my_outcome))
    stop(sprintf("The outcome in your formula is '%s' but you preregistered '%s'. The preregistration is binding, so change the formula to match it.",
                 deparse(formula[[2]]), ch$my_outcome), call. = FALSE)
  want <- c(.main_term(ch), if (ch$my_copredictor == "other") .copred_term(ch))
  got  <- attr(terms(formula), "term.labels")
  if (!setequal(got, want))
    stop(sprintf("Right-hand side mismatch: you wrote { %s } but your preregistration implies { %s }.%s",
                 paste(got, collapse = ", "), paste(want, collapse = ", "),
                 if (.main_term(ch) == "log(unemp)" && !"log(unemp)" %in% got)
                   " You preregistered the log form – write log(unemp) in the formula." else ""),
         call. = FALSE)
  if (missing(estimator) || !identical(estimator, ch$my_estimator))
    stop(sprintf("estimator = \"%s\" does not match your preregistered \"%s\".",
                 if (missing(estimator)) "" else estimator, ch$my_estimator), call. = FALSE)
  writeLines(c("Model accepted – it matches your preregistration:",
               paste0("  ", deparse(formula), ", estimated by ", .est_lab(estimator)),
               "  Run it with run_spec(my_model)."))
  structure(list(choices = ch, formula = formula, estimator = estimator), class = "spec_ticket")
}

run_spec <- function(spec) {
  if (missing(spec) || !inherits(spec, "spec_ticket"))
    stop("Pass the object that build_model() returned, e.g. run_spec(my_model).", call. = FALSE)
  now <- .check_choices()
  if (!identical(spec$choices, now))
    stop("The preregistration cell has changed since you built this model – rerun prereg() and build_model() so they agree.",
         call. = FALSE)
  ch  <- spec$choices
  res <- .result(ch)
  .print_result(ch, res, "Your preregistered specification, read from the curve of 864 specifications:",
                aligned = isTRUE(claim_align))
}

# Both submissions of a participant carry one short tag inside the spec label,
# "explore: [amber-otter-42] …", so that the participant can find their own
# circles on the class chart. The tag rides in the free-text label because the
# form and its fields are frozen infrastructure. The same functions sit in
# R/spec_tools.R of the workspace, which keeps the tag in a file; here it lasts
# for the browser session, and a nickname passed to either submission function
# sets it or brings it back after a reload.
.tag_words <- list(
  adj  = c("amber", "azure", "bright", "calm", "coral", "crisp", "dusky", "early",
           "fair", "gentle", "golden", "hazel", "ivory", "jade", "keen", "lively",
           "lunar", "misty", "noble", "olive", "pale", "quiet", "rapid", "rosy",
           "russet", "silver", "snowy", "solar", "sunny", "swift", "velvet", "vivid"),

# A nickname reduced to lower-case ASCII letters, digits and single hyphens,
# at most 24 characters – the only form that the class chart parses.
.clean_tag <- function(x) {
  # iconv on Windows turns these into "?": the Romanian comma-below letters and the eszett
  x <- gsub("ß", "ss", chartr("ȘșȚț", "SsTt", trimws(as.character(x)[1])))
```

## Where the idea comes from {#where-the-idea-comes-from .smaller}

::: {.small}
- **Multiverse analysis** [@SteegenEtAl2016IncreasingTransparencyMultiverse] began with the choices made before any model is fitted, how to code, exclude and combine: build every dataset that a reasonable set of choices could have produced and run the analysis on all of them. The founding paper asks that "it should become standard practice to go beyond a single data set analysis and to acknowledge the multiverse of statistical results", and concedes that doing so "will often be difficult, and to a large extent subjective" (p. 710)
- **Specification curve analysis** [@SimonsohnEtAl2020SpecificationCurveAnalysis] makes the same move for the choices of the model and adds a display, the estimates in order with the choices beneath each one, and a test of the curve as a whole against a null distribution built by permutation
- Behind both stands the **garden of forking paths** [@GelmanLoken2014StatisticalCrisisScience]: one test chosen after looking at the data already has the wrong p-value, and a single path through the garden keeps no record of its branches
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
What you did in Task 4 was to walk three or four paths of that garden and write them down, which every published analysis could do and almost none reports.
:::

::: notes

Multiverse analysis is Steegen and colleagues in 2016, and it grew out of the choices made before any model is fitted, with the proposal that you build every dataset that a reasonable set of choices could have produced and report the whole set of results. The founding paper asks for that to become standard practice, and concedes in the same breath that it is difficult and to a large extent subjective, which the critics would later press. ## Enumeration and curation {#enumeration-and-curation .smaller}

::: {.small}
Rohrer, Hullman and Gelman ask what a multiverse is *for*, and name three uses, "as a tool for reflection and critique, as a persuasive tool, as a serious inferential tool"; it "fails as a persuasive tool when researchers disagree about which variations should be included in the analysis", and "fails as a serious inferential tool when the included analyses do not target a coherent estimand" [@RohrerEtAl2026WhatsMultiverseGood, p. 1]

- **Enumerate**: cross every option of every decision. Complete and mechanical, and the set fills with specifications that nobody would defend, so that the spread stops meaning anything. Our fourteen decisions multiplied out give about **1,728,000** specifications, each testable under several inference rules
- **Curate**: keep only what you would defend in print, for an estimand that you have named. The set becomes a claim of its own, which a sceptic can attack option by option, so the reasons go beside the curve
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
The curve of the claim is a curated **864**: every option was asked whether it answers *this* claim in a justifiable way, because "there is nothing in the distribution of estimates per se that tells us which is the true effect" [@YoungCumberworth2025MultiverseAnalysisComputational, p. 119]
:::

## Dependence among the estimates {#not-864-tests .smaller}

::: {.small}
- Every specification reuses the **same 270 country-years**, so the estimates share their noise: '77.2% below zero with CR2 p < 0.05' **describes** the curve and is not a p-value for the claim. Clustered errors allow for the years of one country within each fit, and clustering does not make the fits independent of one another
- A test of the whole curve has to build its own null: **shuffle the unemployment and growth series of each country in time**, jointly, refit all 864 specifications, repeat **B = 500** times, and set the observed curve among the 500 null curves
- With B = 500 the smallest reportable p is 2/(B + 1) ≈ 0.004, a floor set by the number of draws, and near p = 0.05 the Monte Carlo error is about ±0.01, so p = 0.04 and p = 0.06 are the same finding

## Critics of the multiverse {#the-critics .smaller}

::: {.small}
- **The pruning critique.** "Multiverse analyses are only informative when all included models represent equally plausible strategies for estimating the same estimand" [@Auspurg2025RobustnessBetterAssessed, p. 1], written in reply to a study of 3.6 billion estimates [@GanslmeierVlandas2025EstimatingExtentSources]; in the red-card study, Auspurg and Brüderl had traced most of the disagreement among the 29 teams to four different estimands [@AuspurgBruderl2021HasCredibilitySocial]
- **One correct analysis.** Once the auxiliary assumptions are fixed, "there is a fact of the matter about which analysis correctly implements that test" [@LakensEtAl2026ThereOnlyOne, p. 7], and "Scientists should not compute the percentage of agreement across different data-analytic strategies, because we do not resolve scientific disagreement by majority vote" (p. 16)
- **What is it for?** "as a tool for reflection and critique, as a persuasive tool, as a serious inferential tool" [@RohrerEtAl2026WhatsMultiverseGood, p. 1], each needing a differently built set
:::

You then became the sixth analyst, varied one decision at a time, put the analysis that you would defend on the class chart, and read your own place among eight hundred and sixty-four justifiable analyses of the same data, which is a publishable way to report a robustness check. It describes every justifiable analysis of the data in hand, and it is only as good as the menu written for it; a test of the whole curve, a declared analysis and a replication on new data are steps that it leaves to others.
